title: Second Language
tagline: The New York Times crossword replaced its entire private vocabulary in a single year, and kept exactly the same letters.
blurb: Every answer the New York Times crossword has printed since 1942 - 2.46 million of them - sorted into the words the puzzle retired and the words it invented. Fifty-six answers were used at least fifty times before 1980 and have not appeared once since 1999; a hundred and sixty-one had never been printed before 1980 and are now used at least fifty times. The median retired word was last seen in 1993 and the median invented word first appeared in 1994, the year Will Shortz took the editor's chair from Eugene Maleska. What did not change is the letters: the Farrar-era and Shortz-era letter distributions correlate at r = 0.997, and crossword answers have been 40.7% to 42.7% vowels in every single year since 1942, against 37.1% for English. Look up any of the 20,000 most-used answers and watch its eighty-four years.
